To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the composition of respiratory supercomplexes is cell type specific and that the 3695G>A mutation in ND1 affects the formation of super-complex I + III + IV, which is associated with decreased cellular respiration.

(1) supercomplex In +IIIn +IVn is conserved in various human and mouse cells, (2) a novel supercomplex In +IIn +IVn with the lowest complex I is associated with complex IV, and (3) this novel supercomplex is impaired in a patient with Leigh’s syndrome.

supercomplex In +IIIn + IVn, which is the only supercomplex that can directly transfer NADH electrons to oxygen, is formed by a minimal supercomplex, termed “lowest complex,” in some, but all of the human cells, and that the 3696G>A mutation in NADH deydrogenase 1 in one patient with mitochondrial disease specifically affects the assembly of this supercomplex containing lowest complex, leading to decreased respiratory chain function and disease phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of the respiratory chain complexes and their supercomplexes.
the assembly of respiratory complexes and supercomplexes and the effect of the mutation in ND1 gene in human disease.
the cell-type-specific modulation of respiratory chain supercomplex organization and the effect of the 3697 G > A mutation in mitochondrial-encoded ND1 on supercomplex assembly and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supercomplexes In + IIIn and In + IIIn+IVn are cell type-dependent.
the composition of respiratory supercomplexes is well conserved among various mouse and human cells and that the presence of LSC is associated with complex IV.
supercomplexes are highly cell type-specific and the formation of super-complex In + IIIn+IVn is not a universal phenomenon in human and mouse cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supercomplex In + IIn + IVn can be composed of two types of LSC In and In + II, which can be modulated by cell type-specific manner.
the composition of respiratory chain supercomplexes in various cell lines is well conserved and that LSC is a key component for the formation of super-complex In + IIIn.
the organization of respiratory chain supercomplexes is not only affected by genetic background but is also cell type specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the composition of respiratory supercomplexes can be modulated in a cell type-specific manner, and that the assembly of supermolecular complexes is a critical determinant of mitochondrial respiratory function.
the organization of the respiratory chain is highly conserved among various cell types and the assembly of supermolecular structures is important for the maintenance of respiratory chain function.

cell type-dependent modulation of the supercomplex composition is a general phenomenon in mammalian cells and the formation of supermolecular complexes in mitochondria is a highly flexible and dynamic process.
